The Chair opened the meeting at 10:05 a.m. and welcomed all members to the inaugural session of the Maintenance Coordination Committee (MCC).

The Chair tabled the MCC Charter (version 1.0, dated 14 July 2003). It was noted that the Maintenance Coordination Committee (MCC) established_date 2003-07-14 date. Record status: current. The Charter had been endorsed by the Executive Director, Infrastructure, following consultation with the Regional Maintenance Managers and the Safety & Standards Directorate.

The Chair drew attention to the following key provisions of the Charter:

- The MCC is a standing committee reporting to the Executive Director, Infrastructure.
- Membership comprises the managers listed in Item 1 above, or their nominated alternates.
- The MCC shall meet monthly, unless otherwise agreed by the Chair.
- The quorum shall be seven (7) members.
- The MCC’s primary function is to coordinate maintenance activities across track, signals, civil, overhead wiring, and rolling stock interfaces to minimise network disruption and ensure safety.

*Discussion:*  
Mr. Ferris queried whether the Charter’s reference to “rolling stock maintenance interface” gave the MCC authority over fleet maintenance scheduling. The Chair clarified that the MCC’s role is coordination and interface management only; direct operational control of fleet maintenance remains with the Fleet Maintenance Manager.

Mr. Okafor requested that the Charter include a provision for the early circulation of maintenance plans to allow for adequate technical review. The Chair agreed that this would be considered as a standing item at the next meeting.

*Key provisions of the adopted Standing Orders:*

- Meetings shall be conducted in accordance with the agenda circulated at least five (5) working days prior to the meeting.
- Decisions shall be made by consensus where possible; where a formal vote is required, a simple majority of members present shall carry the motion.
- The Chair shall have a casting vote in the event of a tie.
- Minutes shall be circulated within ten (10) working days of the meeting.
- Members may raise urgent matters under “Other Business” at the discretion of the Chair.

The two medium-severity incidents (INC-23-0156 and INC-23-0163) are being reviewed by the Regional Safety Committee at their July meeting.

**5.2 Lost Time and Restricted Work**

There were no lost-time injuries during June 2023. The last LTI recorded by the Maintenance Division occurred on 14 March 2023 (INC-23-0067, Broadmeadow). As at 30 June 2023, the division has worked 109 consecutive days without an LTI.

The outstanding Lookout Training recertifications relate to two employees in the Country Track Patrol who were on extended leave during June. Their recertification is scheduled for 5 July 2023. The Manual Handling Refresher shortfall is attributed to the training requirement noted in Section 1; all affected staff have been booked into the July session.

**6. WEATHER AND OPERATIONAL IMPACTS**

June 2023 saw above-average rainfall across the Blue Mountains and Hunter Valley regions. The following operational impacts were recorded:

- **Blue Mountains Line:** Heavy rain on 8–9 June resulted in a 40 km/h temporary speed restriction (TSR) between Katoomba and Medlow Bath. The TSR was lifted on 12 June following track inspection. Minor drainage defects were identified and logged for the track geometry rectification program.
- **Main North Line:** Two days of high wind (17–18 June) disrupted ballast cleaning operations near Muswellbrook. The RM900 was shut down for approximately 6 hours on 18 June for safety reasons.
- **Metropolitan area:** No significant weather-related disruptions were recorded.

**7. CROSSING AND LEVEL CROSSING MAINTENANCE**

During June 2023, routine inspections and maintenance were carried out at level crossings across the network as part of the annual program. A total of 214 level crossings were inspected, with 12 requiring follow-up work.

| Crossing Location | Line | Work Undertaken | Date Completed | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cowra Street, Wallerawang | Main Western | Replace worn rubber panels | 2 June 2023 | Complete |
| Bells Line of Road, Richmond | Richmond | Upgrade boom gate motor and controls | 9 June 2023 | Complete |
| Mid Western Highway, Blayney | Main Western | Renewal of warning lights and bells | 15 June 2023 | Complete |
| Old Hume Highway, Mittagong | Main South | Drainage improvement to approach road | 21 June 2023 | Complete |
| Wollar Road, Gulgong | Gwabegar | Surface re-sheeting of crossing | 28 June 2023 | Complete |

One crossing defect remains open. At the Wombeyan Caves Road crossing near Goulburn, the surface is beginning to break up at the rail edge. This was identified during a routine inspection on 27 June 2023 and logged as defect CW-23-0142. Re-sheeting is planned for the week commencing 17 July 2023, subject to plant availability. A temporary 20 km/h speed restriction has been applied across the crossing in the interim.

**8. PLANT AND EQUIPMENT UTILISATION**

The following table summarises utilisation of major items of plant across the Maintenance Division during June 2023.

| Plant Item | Location | Utilisation % | Availability % | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RM900 Ballast Cleaner | Muswellbrook | 84% | 92% | 6 hours lost to weather on 18 June |
| RRV 21-014 | Broadmeadow | 76% | 95% | Routine service completed |
| RRV 21-022 | Goulburn | 81% | 88% | Awaiting replacement hydraulic hose |
| High Rail Crane 17-003 | Junee | 62% | 97% | Scheduled maintenance, 2 days |
| Tamper T-12 | Bathurst | 73% | 90% | Extended service at Chullora |

The RM900 recorded its highest monthly utilisation since February 2023, reflecting the progress of the ballast cleaning program on the Main North Line. The shortfall against 100% availability relates to the weather shutdown noted in Section 6.

RRV 21-022 is currently operating with a temporary hydraulic hose repair. The replacement hose is on order and expected to arrive by 12 July 2023. The machine is restricted to non-critical tasks until the replacement is fitted.

**9. BUDGET AND RESOURCE CONSUMPTION**

Expenditure against the maintenance budget for June 2023 is summarised below. All figures exclude GST.

| Cost Centre | June Budget ($'000) | June Actual ($'000) | Variance ($'000) | YTD Variance ($'000) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Track Maintenance – Metropolitan | 1,240 | 1,182 | 58 Fav | 214 Fav |
| Track Maintenance – Country | 1,890 | 2,041 | 151 Adv | 96 Adv |
| Structures Maintenance | 720 | 688 | 32 Fav | 145 Fav |
| Signals and Electrical | 940 | 915 | 25 Fav | 88 Fav |
| Plant and Equipment | 610 | 598 | 12 Fav | 41 Fav |
| Level Crossings | 380 | 402 | 22 Adv | 17 Fav |
| **Total** | **5,780** | **5,826** | **46 Adv** | **409 Fav** |

The adverse variance in Country Track Maintenance is primarily attributable to the urgent ballast cleaning work on the Main North Line following the June weather events, and the associated hire of additional ballast wagons. The favourable YTD position remains within the division's target range.

Overtime hours for the month totalled 1,847, compared with a budget of 1,600. The additional hours were largely incurred in the Blue Mountains and Muswellbrook areas in response to the weather-related repairs. Overtime is expected to return to normal levels in July.
